title: introduce-cost-slo-prober-with-cold-prefetch-and-split-batcher
author: Maya Kim
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for mixed-latency workloads while preserving p99 latency SLOs by combining an empirical cost-SLO prober, a cold-cache prefetcher for KV-heavy prompts, and a split-batcher that dynamically decides between size- and latency-optimized microbatches. This PR wires a lightweight probing loop into the runtime optimizer, exposes safe default profiles, and adds metrics and canary flags. Changes are designed to be opt-in via config flags and non-breaking for existing deployments. Checklist: [x] implement prober loop and SDK flags; [x] add cold prefetch hook and cache TTL tuning; [x] add split-batcher with heuristics for long and short sequences; [x] add unit tests and integration canary; [x] add docs snippet and console feature flag. Impact: expected unit cost reduction for conversational workloads with 1-2 sentence prompts (10-25%) and for long-context retrieval scenarios (5-15%) at minimal p99 regressions under typical load. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and dashboard updates.

release_notes: Introduce cost-SLO prober (opt-in) with cold-cache prefetch and a split-batcher that chooses size- or latency-optimized microbatches; metrics and console flags added; recommended canary before global enable.
testing_notes: Local unit tests added for prober and split-batcher; ran integration canary against a 5-node canary cluster using representative conversation and retrieval workloads; observed expected token savings without p99 regressions in canary window.
rollback_plan: Feature flags allow immediate disable; remove prober trials and revert to last pinned profile. In severe regressions: disable prefetch and split-batcher via console and rollback config to previous cost_profiles.yaml.
notes_for_release_engineer: Schedule gradual ramp: 0.5% customers -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over two weeks; monitor econ.prober.best_profile_change and p99 latency alarms; ensure private deployments have prefetch disabled unless explicitly enabled.
